Quality Dimensions

Performance

Performance refers to a product's primary operating characteristics. This dimension of quality involves measurable attributes; brands can usually be ranked objectively on individual aspects of performance.

Features

Features are additional characteristics that enhance the appeal of the product or service to the user.

Reliability

Reliability is the likelihood that a product will not fail within a specific time period. This is a key element for users who need the product to work without fail.

Conformance

Conformance is the precision with which the product or service meets the specified standards.

Durability

Serviceability

Aesthetics

Aesthetics is the subjective dimension indicating the kind of response a user has to a product. It represents the individual’s personal preference.

Perceived Quality

Perceived Quality is the quality attributed to a good or service based on indirect measures.

Warning: Do You Recognize these Five Common Piles of Prepper BS

The author appears to have a good handle on things. Most of his points are arguable and depend on the situation though.

"The Golden Horde" - planning to succeed against something like that is pretty much impossible on an individual basis. If your family is hit by a mass of people you're bound to lose; surrender might mean survival and fighting would take some of them with you but would almost certainly result in your death. Better to plan for small bands of raiders instead.

"Shoot first" - really depends on the situation and what news you've received. Taking long shots at an approaching person or group isn't neighborly.

"Bugging out to the woods" - The author goes into one versus the other, but it's not mentioned that, if you choose hunkering down as your primary strategy, there's no reason not to prepare for both; it costs very little additional resources, and the situation might mean you'd be better off running.
I agree, bugging in or bugging out are not solutions by themselves. You need to be prepared for both and getting wrapped up in super scripted scenarios is a trap that can get you killed.

Most of it is on the money. I'm seeing some of it with the Harvey aftermath in Houston right now. There are a few isolated instances of looting and shooting, but for the most part there is complete law and order (or as much order as you can have with so many people displaced and people running around providing rescues). Yesterday, the cops were out ALL over making a huge public show. It was great. They were crazy tired, but they weren't being jerks and the worst lawlessness I saw were people making rolling stops at intersections where there were no other vehicles. But before yesterday, the cops were busy doing rescues and other stuff more important than being seen. And the citizens were out instead. I was rolling with my rifle next to me in my truck (mostly because I was had to go through parts of town that aren't the best in good times), but never came close to needing it. Even in the less good areas, people were out everywhere, either helping each other or just walking and watching.

One factor in all this is that the electricity stayed on for most people and almost every cell tower stayed on. Almost everyone has easy access to broadcast media and social media. And the official response with regard to getting displaced people into shelters and getting them basic supplies was immediate and thorough. I keep mentally comparing it to what I saw of Katrina from Houston. I really wonder how much of the reported lawlessness was exaggerated (in scale, was it really over that wide of an area?). I wonder how much of the difference that I see in Katrina and Harvey is due to lessons learned and improvements implemented.

Edit: One thing I'd differ with him on is using UHF radios instead of CB. It's probably good to have a CB for interface, but it's more susceptible to interference from atmospheric and solar events and doesn't have the range or flexibility of UHF, though you won't get things like tropo bounce or tunneling... but those are not reliable and talking with someone across an oceans is rarely necessary for an individual. CB antennas are big so it's harder to make multiple well-tuned antennas. You can run UHF comms, like FRS and GMRS with 70 cm equipment and the antennas are relatively tiny (quarter wavelength is about eight inches). The radios are small, cheap, portable, and you can easily run a repeater if you need more range.

Puerto Rico really shows a solid SHTF event. Sure they are getting aid, but honestly lossing everything hasn't really changed the society. No matter how much it's a hot political topic, it's not chaos or the purge.
